summary: Speaking at New Raman Reti (Alachua) from Srimad-Bhagavatam 7.5.11, Prahlada Maharaja's prayer, Indradyumna Swami chooses to go back to basics and examine the foundation of devotional life, chanting Hare Krishna, arguing that humility is its most essential ingredient, the sugar in the cake without which the chanting cannot yield its full fruit. He reviews the stages of chanting (offensive, clearing, and offenseless or pure) and of bhakti (from sraddha through bhava and prema), noting that the ultimate fruit of the holy name is prema and even vipralambha-bhava, the feeling of separation that Haridasa Thakura and Mahaprabhu express in the Siksastakam. The heart of the talk is Siksastakam verse 3 (trinad api sunicena), to chant thinking oneself lower than a straw, more tolerant than a tree, free of false prestige and offering all respect to others, which he calls Prabhupada's formula for love of God, illustrated by Prabhupada telling his godbrother Dr. O.B.L. Kapoor in his chemical lab that he knew the formula but did not know how to apply it, and which Mahaprabhu personally gave both to the assembled devotees in Adi-lila 17 and to Raghunatha dasa Goswami in Antya-lila. Because humility's opposite is pride, he analyzes what devotees are falsely proud of, the body (a prisoner's stripes, a sign of independence from Krishna), possessions, and above all their own achievements in devotional service, warning that attachment to fame is the hardest thing to renounce, shown by his Kumbha Mela account of renunciate sadhus parading proudly on elephants and a Shankaracharya-follower's beautiful Krishna-katha spoiled by the impersonal conclusion tat tvam asi. He insists devotees can take no credit because they are only instruments in the hands of guru and Krishna (the dull-versus-sharp-knife analogy, Prabhupada blushing and crediting his Guru Maharaja, and the punar musiko bhava story of a mouse turned into cat, dog, and tiger and then back into a mouse), and that the Lord even strips away opulence to keep His devotees humble, as when Arjuna lost his weapons and was defeated by cowherds after Krishna's departure, and as Kunti prays that the Lord is approached only by the materially exhausted. He closes with practical means to uproot pride: living simply through yukta-vairagya (taking by need not greed, and the reminder that even the body belongs to Krishna, as Mahaprabhu forbade Sanatana Goswami to end his life), serving other Vaishnavas menially (King Prataparudra sweeping the road with a golden broom to win Mahaprabhu's embrace), voluntarily accepting a lowly position, and going out on sankirtana where no one offers you guru-puja, the natural school of humility, recalling Prabhupada chanting and selling fifty copies of Easy Journey to Other Planets in a Mexico City park in 1973.
key_points: Humility is the essential ingredient of pure chanting, the sugar in the cake; its opposite, pride, must be removed to chant the holy name effectively and progress toward prema.

Siksastakam verse 3 (trinad api sunicena) is the central formula for love of God, given by Mahaprabhu to all devotees (CC Adi 17) and to Raghunatha dasa Goswami (CC Antya); Prabhupada humbly added that he knew the formula but not how to apply it.

Devotees falsely take pride in the body, possessions, and especially their own devotional achievements and fame; fame is the hardest attachment to give up (Kumbha Mela sadhus on elephants, and the Shankaracharya-follower's tat tvam asi).

We can claim no credit; we are mere instruments of guru and Krishna (dull vs. sharp knife, BG 11.34 be but an instrument), and Krishna even removes powers and opulence to keep devotees humble (Arjuna defeated by cowherds after losing his weapons).

Practical antidotes to pride include simple living and yukta-vairagya (take by need not greed, everything belongs to Krishna) and menial service to Vaishnavas (Prataparudra sweeping the road with a golden broom to earn Mahaprabhu's embrace).

Street sankirtana is the natural training ground for humility, since no one offers you guru-puja there, and it reminds us we are not better than others, only more fortunate (CC Madhya 19.151, brahmanda bhramite).
The goal of humble chanting is one day to see, with spiritual eyes, the divine form of Sri Sri Radha-Shyamasundara.
references: Srimad-Bhagavatam 7.5.11 (Prahlada Maharaja's prayer) - obeisances to the Lord whose external energy creates the distinctions of friend and enemy; the class verse.

Bhagavad-gita 5.18 (vidya-vinaya-sampanne... panditah sama-darsinah) - the learned see with equal vision a brahmana, cow, elephant, dog, and dog-eater; quoted in Prabhupada's purport on Vaishnava humility.

Siksastakam verse 3 (trinad api sunicena taror api sahisnuna, amanina manadena kirtaniyah sada harih) - the central verse; chant humbly, lower than a straw, more tolerant than a tree; also appears in Caitanya-caritamrta Adi-lila 17 and Antya-lila.
Siksastakam verse 7 (yugayitam nimesena... govinda-virahena me) - feeling Your separation I take a moment to be twelve years; cited as the fruit of chanting, vipralambha-bhava, per Haridasa Thakura.
Siksastakam verse 4 (na dhanam na janam na sundarim kavitam va... bhaktir ahaituki tvayi) - I want no wealth, followers, or beautiful women, only causeless devotional service birth after birth.

Caitanya-caritamrta Antya-lila, instructions to Raghunatha dasa Goswami (gramya-katha na sunibe...) - do not hear mundane talk, eat palatable food, or dress nicely, expect no honor but offer respect, always chant and mentally serve Radha-Krishna in Vrindavana; likely Antya 6.236-237.

Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu (Rupa Goswami) - the ladder of devotional stages: adau sraddha, sadhu-sanga, bhajana-kriya, anartha-nivrtti, nistha, ruci, asakti, bhava, prema (approx. 1.4.15-16); he quotes the first half.
Bhagavad-gita 3.37 - lust (kama) is the all-devouring sinful enemy of this world; referenced regarding renunciates freed from lust.
Bhagavad-gita 11.33-34 - Therefore get up, Arjuna... be but an instrument (nimitta-matram), O Savyasaci; on being an instrument of the Lord.
Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.8.26 (Kunti's prayers, janmaisvarya-sruta-sribhih) - the Lord is approached only by the materially exhausted, not by those proud of birth, wealth, education, or beauty.
Srimad-Bhagavatam 5.5.8 (Rsabhadeva, pumsah striya mithuni-bhavam) - male-female attraction is the knot binding one to body, home, and the sense of I and mine.

Caitanya-caritamrta Madhya 19.151 (brahmanda bhramite kona bhagyavan jiva, guru-krsna-prasade paya bhakti-lata-bija) - wandering through the universe, a fortunate soul receives the seed of the bhakti creeper by the mercy of guru and Krishna.
Sri Isopanisad, Mantra 1 (isavasyam idam sarvam... tena tyaktena bhunjithah) - everything is controlled by the Lord; take only your quota and do not be greedy; basis for simple living.
Srimad-Bhagavatam, Third Canto, Brahma's prayer to give up the false prestige of being the creator (tasminn...) - likely SB 3.9.24; cited as a model of humility.

Srimad-Bhagavatam, Tenth Canto, Brahma-vimohana-lila - Brahma's prayers after stealing Krishna's cows and boys, that those who claim to know everything about Krishna may think so, while His opulences are beyond mind and body; exact verse number uncertain.
Raghunatha dasa Goswami's prayer - O mind, a shameless low-born prostitute is dancing in my heart in the form of desire for fame; how can pure love for Krishna find a place there?
Canakya-niti (Canakya Pandita) - one does not find rubies in every mountain, sandalwood in every forest, or genuine sadhus everywhere; if you find them, grab them.
Adi Purana statement quoted by Krishna - one who claims to be My devotee is not; but the devotee of My devotee is truly My devotee.
stories: The formula for love of God — in his pharmaceutical lab Prabhupada tells his godbrother Dr. O.B.L. Kapoor that he has discovered the formula for love of God; it is trinad api sunicena, but he humbly adds, 'I know the formula, but I don't know how to apply it.'
Sugar in the cake — humility is the essential ingredient of pure chanting, like the sugar without which even a beautiful three-inch-iced cake is worthless.
Kumbha Mela sadhus on elephants — renunciates who had given up money and women still seemed to relish being famous, paraded proudly on elephants.

The Shankaracharya-follower's spoiled katha — an austere speaker glorifies baby Krishna so sweetly, then ruins it with the impersonal conclusion 'tat tvam asi' (thou art that Krishna), sending the Maharaja running to bathe.
The prisoner's stripes — the material body is like a convict's black-and-white stripes, a badge of our escape from Krishna, yet we foolishly admire it as beautiful.
Punar musiko bhava — a yogi turns a fearful mouse into a cat, then a dog, then a tiger; when the ungrateful tiger moves to eat him, the yogi says 'again become a mouse.'

Prataparudra's golden broom — the King of Puri, forbidden association as a worldly monarch, humbly sweeps the road before Jagannath's chariot with a golden broom and thereby wins Mahaprabhu's embrace.

Arjuna defeated by cowherds — after Krishna returns to the spiritual world, the mighty Arjuna, escorting the gopis, loses his divine powers and is beaten by simple forest-dwellers with sticks, teaching that his strength was Krishna's all along.
quotes: Deathlessness begins at the moment of initiation.
we are what we are only by the mercy of guru.
You take one step towards God, he takes a thousand steps.
the best gift we can give our spiritual master is our progress in Krishna consciousness.
we're not better than others but we are certainly more fortunate than them.
